title: DC-area forecast: A break in the rain and gustiest wind late tonight. Breezy with light showers Sunday.
contentHtml:
Always a human at the helm: Updated around-the-clock by Capital Weather meteorologists.

Happening now: Late afternoon and evening temperatures dip from the 60s toward mid-50s to near 60 for predawn lows. The steadiest, heaviest showers—along with the gustiest winds—should ease, giving us a partial lull from about midnight into morning.

What's next? Breezes and showers may increase again by late morning Sunday, lasting through much of the afternoon. Showers look mainly light and scattered. Gradually brighter skies and calmer conditions early week.

Forecast in detail

Tonight: Showers, locally heavier at times, continue into the evening before becoming more scattered and easing by and after midnight. Breezes continue from the north—with a couple of gusts near 30 mph possible early evening—before gusts ease slightly. Wettest and windiest spots still favor east and northeast of DC. Lows in the mid-50s to near 60. Confidence: Medium

Tomorrow (Sunday): Mostly cloudy and cool, with mainly light, scattered showers, especially very late morning into at least mid-afternoon. Dry intervals are likely at times too. Breezy from the northwest, with a couple of gusts near 30 mph. Highs in the upper 50s to mid-60s. Confidence: Medium

Hourly Forecast | Pollen, Air & UV

Tomorrow night: Cloudy skies stick around, with a slight chance of a lingering shower. Winds stay breezy from the northwest but gradually ease. Temperatures may prove relatively steady in the mid-50s to around 60. Confidence: Medium

A look ahead

Skies are mostly cloudy Monday as highs reach the upper 60s to low 70s. Breezes gradually decrease. Confidence: Medium

Skies start to clear Tuesday, with a mix of sun and clouds continuing into Wednesday. Highs climb back into the mid- to upper 70s both days, with light winds around 5 to 10 mph. Confidence: Medium

Today’s daily digit — 5/10: At least the morning is dry before shower chances increase this afternoon. | 🤚 Your call?
The digit is a somewhat subjective rating of the day’s weather, on a 0-to-10 scale.

DC weather history for September 26

Intense late-season heat in 1930 pushed temperatures to 96 degrees, capping a brutal summer marked by persistent 90s and a historic drought.
